evidence.description: The notification observer closure captures 'self' weakly but calls 'handleAuthenticationCompletion' which is an actor-isolated method, potentially leading to unexpected behavior if the actor is deallocated or if the closure is executed on a non-isolated context.

candidates.explanation: The notification observer is added to the notification center with a queue of .main, but the manager is an actor. While the closure captures 'self' weakly, the call to 'handleAuthenticationCompletion' (an actor method) inside a closure that might not be properly synchronized with the actor's internal state can lead to issues, although the actor's isolation usually handles the entry point.
candidates.title: Potential Actor Isolation Mismatch in Notification Observer

evidence.description: A new Task is created inside 'handlePageLoadCompletion' which captures 'self' weakly and calls 'handleAuthenticationCompletion' after a sleep.

candidates.explanation: Every time a page load notification is received for an invisible tab, a new asynchronous Task is spawned. If notifications arrive rapidly, this could lead to an accumulation of pending tasks, potentially causing performance degradation or race conditions in handling the tab closure.
candidates.title: Unbounded Task Creation

evidence.description: The key for the page load observer is constructed using a string suffix: "\(tab.tabUUID)_pageload".
The cleanup logic relies on the same string suffix to identify and remove the page load observer.

candidates.explanation: The manager uses string concatenation to store multiple observers for the same tab in a single dictionary. This approach is error-prone and relies on consistent string formatting across different methods (setup and cleanup).
candidates.title: Fragile String-Based Key Management

evidence.description: The 'removeTab' method takes a completion handler that performs several operations including selecting a new tab and cleaning up tracking.

candidates.explanation: The completion handler for 'removeTab' performs significant logic, including state changes (selecting a tab) and logging. This can make the flow of execution harder to trace and may lead to issues if 'removeTab' is called from multiple contexts.
candidates.title: Side Effects in Completion Handler
